implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — THE PER-GOAL RESOLVER, a new module apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts (≤250 lines) plus its bridge affordance-planning-offers.js (`export * from "./affordance-planning-offers.ts";`, byte-identical to the sibling bridges in apps/daemon/src/http). Export `resolvePlanningOffers(input: { ledger: DurableLedger; projectId: string; mintId: () => string }): { offers: readonly NextAllowedCommand[]; planningGoalRefs: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }`.
Enumerate durable goals by scanning `ledger.aggregates` for records with `goalId === aggregateId`, `projectId === input.projectId` and a string `planningRunRef` (the same predicate as durableGoalMatches, minus the run pin), sorted by goalId for determinism. For each goal G with run R: `planningGoalRefs[R] = planningGoalRef(ledger, projectId, R)` when non-null (move `planningGoalRef`/`durableGoalMatches`/`record` into this module and re-export or import them back into affordance-read.ts — one implementation, two callers, no copy). Offer readiness is PER RUN, decided by the same predicates affordance-read.ts uses today but evaluated against R and G instead of the global `ledger.kinds`: plan.propose at R while `planReviewable(ledger, R)` is false (mirror effectiveLedger :82-91, which is the per-run reading of "committed"); approval.decide at R when the plan is reviewable and the run's durable state shows no decided approval (measure the run state's lifecycle vocabulary via `stateOf(ledger, R)` before choosing the predicate — record it); goal.close at G when its run's approval is decided and the goal is not yet closed (measure goal state for the closed marker). Each offer is built with the SAME `offer(kind, aggregateId, version, BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA_VERSION)` shape (commandEnvelopeVersion, commandId minted per read, expectedVersion = versionOf(ledger, aggregateId), inputSchemaVersion, targetAggregateId) — pass the `offer` builder in or reconstruct it identically; do not add keys to NextAllowedCommand (the offer shape is pinned by control-room tests you do not own). No goal-scan cap is added here; the catalog's 256-row cap (goal-catalog-read.ts:15, task-3f71ba30) is a catalog concern, not the surface's.
implementationPlan.note: Added 132-line per-goal resolver + runtime bridge. Measured lifecycle vocabulary before coding: run state.state.lifecycle=PLAN_REVIEW is the reviewable marker; approval.decide does not mutate the run—it persists GoalExecutionEnabled on the bound goal and moves GoalState.lifecycle DRAFT→EXECUTION_ENABLED; goal.close moves the goal to COMPLETED. Resolver therefore offers approval at a reviewable run only while its validated bound goal is DRAFT, and close only for EXECUTION_ENABLED/CLOSING goals. Duplicate run bindings and mismatched run goalRef fail closed with no map entry/offer. Step-2 production-surface tests remain intentionally red until step-4 wiring.
